hub_triggers.eng:design: Code crossing a function boundary → the **architect** skill, parallel design exploration before implementing.
hub_triggers.eng:ground: Nontrivial change, architecture decision, or "are we sure?" → the **how** skill.
hub_triggers.eng:ship.before: Before commit → the `deslop` skill from the `cursor-team-kit` plugin (`/deslop`).

adapter.claude:
pstack skills use Cursor names. In Claude Code, map each Cursor name in a skill with the tables below. `<skills>` means the folder that holds this `craft/` folder. rig installs each pstack skill at `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md`. If a Cursor field has no row, drop it and say so. Never pass a field or value that the tool schema rejects.

### Tools

| Cursor | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| `Task` | `Agent` |
| `AskQuestion` | `AskUserQuestion`. In `-p` mode it is absent, so ask in plain text. |
| Open a todolist | Use `TodoWrite` if the session offers it. Otherwise keep the list in your reply and update it at each phase. |
| Run another pstack skill (`/name` or "the **name** skill") | `Read` `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md` and follow it. The `Skill` tool refuses these skills, because rig hides them from the model. When you tell the user to type it, write `/<name>`. |
| `Grep`, `Glob` | `Bash` with `rg` when the session has no `Grep` or `Glob`. |

### Subagent fields

| Cursor | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent_type: generalPurpose` | `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` |
| `poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko` | `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"`, `subagent_type: "comment-sicko"`. rig installs both in `~/.claude/agents/`. |
| `readonly: true` | `subagent_type: "Explore"`. It keeps `Bash`, so the brief also says "do not edit files", and you check `git status` afterward. |
| `readonly: false` | `general-purpose`. It keeps the session's MCP servers. |
| `environment: "cloud"` | `isolation: "worktree"`. Name the branch or commit the worker checks out. |
| `environment: "local"` | Omit. |
| `cloud_base_branch: <b>` | Tell the worker to check out `<b>` first. |
| `run_in_background: true` | Omit. Subagents run in the background by default and notify you when they finish. |
| `resume` | Spawn a new agent and paste the earlier result into its brief. |
| `file_attachments` | List the paths in the brief. |

### Models

| Cursor | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| `claude-<family>-<version>-<effort>[-fast]`, such as `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` | `model: "opus"` and `effort: "xhigh"`. `model` takes only `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`. Drop `-fast`. |
| A `grok-*`, `gpt-*`, or other non-Claude slug | Omit `model` so the agent runs on the session model, and say so. |
| `auto` or `inherit-parent` | Omit `model`. |
| The `pstack-models.mdc` rule, `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` | `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md`. rig writes this file from its model table. Claude Code loads it into every new session, so its role lines are already in context. If they are not, read the file. If the file or the role's line is missing, use the skill's default slug. |
| A role value `<model> <effort>`, such as `opus high` | `model: "opus"` and `effort: "high"`. |

### setup-pstack

rig does not install `setup-pstack`. rig writes `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md` from the model table of the rig config. When a step names `setup-pstack`, tell the user to change the model table with `rig models set` and to run `rig apply`. Do not write the rule file yourself.

### Paths

| Cursor | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| `.cursor/skills/`, `~/.cursor/skills/` | `.claude/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/` |
| `~/.cursor/plugins/`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | rig installs pstack as skills, not as a plugin. |
| The `SKILL.md` of the `poteto-mode` skill | `<skills>/craft/hub.md`. Put its absolute path in every `poteto-agent` brief. |
| `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, always-applied rules | `CLAUDE.md`, or `AGENTS.md` when no `CLAUDE.md` exists. Claude Code never reads `.mdc` files. The model rule is the exception. See Models. |
| `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/<path>` | `<skills>/<name>/<rest>` when `<path>` is `skills/<name>/<rest>` and that file exists. rig does not install `docs/` or `README.md`. Never fetch the URL. Give the user the URL when they need a link. |
| Transcripts in `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/` | `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl`. The slug is the workspace path with each `/` and `.` changed to `-`, so `/Users/you/proj` is `-Users-you-proj`. The newest `.jsonl` directly in that folder is the current session. Its `<session>/subagents/` folder holds subagent transcripts. Read only this workspace's folder. |

### Cursor-only features

Claude Code has no Cursor Automations, Bugbot, Cursor cloud agents, or built-in PR tool. When a step needs one, put one line in your reply, `Skipped in Claude Code: <step>. <reason>.`, then go on to the next step. Do not stop, ask, or retry. When a later step needs what the skipped step made, such as a URL or a key, leave a placeholder and name it in the line.

| Cursor | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| Cursor Automations: routines, `update_state` routine calls, `api2.cursor.sh/automations` webhooks, routine wakes, and `SendToUser` secret requests | Skip with the line. |
| Bugbot | Bugbot comments on a GitHub PR are ordinary review threads, so triage them with the forge command that the step gives. Skip a step that starts, waits for, or configures Bugbot when the PR has no Bugbot check or comment. |
| Cursor cloud agents | `environment: "cloud"` maps to a worktree, as in Subagent fields. Skip a step that needs the cloud agent itself, such as its dashboard status or its own machine. |
| A built-in PR tool | Use the forge command that the step gives, such as `gh pr create`. That is not a skip, so write no line. |
adapter.codex:
pstack skills use Cursor names. In Codex, map each Cursor name in a skill with the tables below. `<skills>` means the folder that holds this `craft/` folder. rig installs each pstack skill at `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md`. If a Cursor field has no row, drop it and say so. Never pass a field or value that the tool schema rejects.

### Tools

| Cursor | Codex |
| --- | --- |
| `Task` | `spawn_agent`. Collect the result with `wait_agent`. Send more input with `send_input`. Stop the agent with `close_agent`. If the session has no `spawn_agent`, do the work yourself in order, and say so. |
| `AskQuestion` | `request_user_input` if the session offers it. Otherwise ask in one short numbered list in your reply. |
| Open a todolist | `update_plan`. |
| Run another pstack skill (`/name` or "the **name** skill") | Read `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md` and follow it. When you tell the user to type it, write `$<name>`. |
| `Grep`, `Glob` | `exec_command` with `rg`, or with `rg --files` for a file list. |

### Subagent fields

| Cursor | Codex |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent_type: generalPurpose` | `agent_type: "default"` |
| `poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko` | `agent_type: "poteto-agent"`, `agent_type: "comment-sicko"`. rig installs both in `~/.codex/agents/`. |
| `readonly: true` | `agent_type: "explorer"`. The brief also says "do not edit files", and you check `git status` afterward. |
| `readonly: false` | `agent_type: "default"`. |
| `environment: "cloud"` | Codex has no worktree field. Tell the worker to make a git worktree of the branch or commit, and to work only in it. |
| `environment: "local"` | Omit. |
| `cloud_base_branch: <b>` | Tell the worker to check out `<b>` first. |
| `run_in_background: true` | Omit. `spawn_agent` returns at once. Collect the result with `wait_agent`. |
| `resume` | Use `send_input` if the agent is still open. Otherwise spawn a new agent and paste the earlier result into its message. |
| `file_attachments` | List the paths in the message. |

### Models

| Cursor | Codex |
| --- | --- |
| A model slug that a skill names, `auto`, or `inherit-parent` | Omit `model` and `reasoning_effort`, unless the next row gives the role's line. The spawned agent then uses the session model. Say so when the skill named a slug. |
| The `pstack-models.mdc` rule, `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` | `~/.codex/pstack-models.md`. rig writes this file from its model table. Read the role line there, such as `swarm workers: gpt-6.1-terra high`, and pass its `model` and `reasoning_effort` to `spawn_agent`. The operator set this table with `rig models set`, so it counts as the user's request to set `model`. If the file or the role's line is missing, follow the row above. |

### setup-pstack

rig does not install `setup-pstack`. When a step names `setup-pstack`, tell the user to change the model table with `rig models set` and to run `rig apply`. Do not write a rule file yourself.

### Paths

| Cursor | Codex |
| --- | --- |
| `.cursor/skills/`, `~/.cursor/skills/` | `.agents/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, `~/.codex/skills/` |
| `~/.cursor/plugins/`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | rig installs pstack as skills, not as a plugin. |
| The `SKILL.md` of the `poteto-mode` skill | `<skills>/craft/hub.md`. Put its absolute path in every `poteto-agent` message. |
| `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, always-applied rules | `AGENTS.md`. Codex never reads `.mdc` files. |
| `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/<path>` | `<skills>/<name>/<rest>` when `<path>` is `skills/<name>/<rest>` and that file exists. rig does not install `docs/` or `README.md`. Never fetch the URL. Give the user the URL when they need a link. |
| Transcripts in `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/` | `~/.codex/sessions/`. Each session is one `rollout-*.jsonl` file in a dated folder. The newest file is the current session. |

### Cursor-only features

Codex has no Cursor Automations, Bugbot, Cursor cloud agents, or built-in PR tool. When a step needs one, put one line in your reply, `Skipped in Codex: <step>. <reason>.`, then go on to the next step. Do not stop, ask, or retry. When a later step needs what the skipped step made, leave a placeholder and name it in the line. For a PR, use the forge command that the step gives, such as `gh pr create`. That is not a skip.

adapter.omp:
pstack skills use Cursor names. In omp, map each Cursor name in a skill with the tables below. `<skills>` means the folder that holds this `craft/` folder. rig installs each pstack skill at `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md`. If a Cursor field has no row, drop it and say so. Never pass a field or value that the tool schema rejects.

### Tools

| Cursor | omp |
| --- | --- |
| `Task` | `task`. Put shared background in `context` and one item for each agent in `tasks`. |
| `AskQuestion` | `ask`, with `questions` and their `options`. |
| Open a todolist | `todo` with `op: "init"`. Then use `op: "start"` and `op: "done"` for each item. |

### Subagent fields

| Cursor | omp |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent_type: generalPurpose` | `agent: "task"` |
| `poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko` | rig installs no agents for omp. Use `agent: "task"`. Put the absolute path of `<skills>/craft/hub.md` in the item's `task`, and tell the agent that it is a delegate of that hub. |
| `readonly: true` | `agent: "scout"`. Its tools only read and search. |
| `readonly: false` | `agent: "task"`. |
| `environment: "cloud"` | `isolated: true` if the schema offers it. Otherwise tell the worker to make a git worktree of the branch or commit, and to work only in it. |
| `environment: "local"` | Omit. |
| `cloud_base_branch: <b>` | Tell the worker to check out `<b>` first. |
| `run_in_background: true` | Omit. omp sets background mode in its own settings. |
| `resume` | Spawn a new agent and paste the earlier result into its `task`. |
| `file_attachments` | List the paths in the item's `task`. |

### Models

| Cursor | omp |
| --- | --- |
| A model slug that a skill names, `auto`, or `inherit-parent` | Omit `model`, unless the next row gives the role's line. omp accepts a per-call `model` only when the operator allows it. Say so when the skill named a slug. |

Read the role line there, such as `swarm workers: google-antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash:high`. Pass its value as `model` only when `task.perCallModel` allows it and, when `task.perCallModelAllow` is set, lists it. Otherwise omit `model` and say so. If the file or the role's line is missing, follow the row above. |

### setup-pstack

rig does not install `setup-pstack`. When a step names `setup-pstack`, tell the user to change the model table with `rig models set` and to run `rig apply`. Do not write a rule file yourself.

| Cursor | omp |
| --- | --- |

| `~/.cursor/plugins/`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | rig installs pstack as skills, not as a plugin. |
| The `SKILL.md` of the `poteto-mode` skill | `<skills>/craft/hub.md`. Put its absolute path in every delegate's `task`. |
| `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, always-applied rules | `AGENTS.md`. omp never reads `.mdc` files. |
| `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/<path>` | `<skills>/<name>/<rest>` when `<path>` is `skills/<name>/<rest>` and that file exists. rig does not install `docs/` or `README.md`. Never fetch the URL. Give the user the URL when they need a link. |
| Transcripts in `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/` | `~/.omp/agent/sessions/`. |

### Cursor-only features

omp has no Cursor Automations, Bugbot, Cursor cloud agents, or built-in PR tool. When a step needs one, put one line in your reply, `Skipped in omp: <step>. <reason>.`, then go on to the next step. Do not stop, ask, or retry. When a later step needs what the skipped step made, leave a placeholder and name it in the line. For a PR, use the forge command that the step gives, such as `gh pr create`. That is not a skip.
adapter.antigravity:
pstack skills use Cursor names. In Antigravity, map each Cursor name in a skill with the tables below. `<skills>` means the folder that holds this `craft/` folder. rig installs each pstack skill at `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md`, and `~/.gemini/config/skills.json` registers `<skills>` with Antigravity. If a Cursor field has no row, drop it and say so. Never pass a field or value that the tool schema rejects.

### Tools

| Cursor | Antigravity |
| --- | --- |
| `Task` | `invoke_subagent`. Put the brief in `Prompt` and the agent name in `TypeName`. |
| `AskQuestion` | `ask_question`. In `agy -p` mode, ask in plain text. |
| Open a todolist | Keep the list in your reply and update it at each phase. |
| Run another pstack skill (`/name` or "the **name** skill") | `view_file` `<skills>/<name>/SKILL.md` and follow it. When you tell the user to type it, write `/<name>`. |
| `Grep`, `Glob` | `grep_search`, `find_by_name`. |

### Subagent fields

| Cursor | Antigravity |
| --- | --- |
| `subagent_type: generalPurpose` | `invoke_subagent` with a built-in `TypeName` that the tool lists. |
| `poteto-agent`, `comment-sicko` | `TypeName: "poteto-agent"`, `TypeName: "comment-sicko"`. rig installs both in `~/.gemini/config/agents/`. |
| `readonly: true` | A built-in `TypeName`. The brief also says "do not edit files", and you check `git status` afterward. |
| `readonly: false` | A built-in `TypeName`. |
| `environment: "cloud"` | Tell the worker to make a git worktree of the branch or commit, and to work only in it. |
| `environment: "local"` | Omit. |
| `cloud_base_branch: <b>` | Tell the worker to check out `<b>` first. |
| `run_in_background: true` | Omit. |
| `resume` | Spawn a new agent and paste the earlier result into its `Prompt`. |
| `file_attachments` | List the paths in the `Prompt`. |

### Models

| Cursor | Antigravity |
| --- | --- |
| A model slug that a skill names, `auto`, or `inherit-parent` | Omit the model. `invoke_subagent` takes no model, and a subagent file names only `inherit`, `flash` or `pro`. Say so when the skill named a slug. |
| The `pstack-models.mdc` rule, `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` | rig writes no model rule for Antigravity. Follow the row above for every role. |

### setup-pstack

rig does not install `setup-pstack`. When a step names `setup-pstack`, tell the user to change the model table with `rig models set` and to run `rig apply`. Do not write a rule file yourself.

### Paths

| Cursor | Antigravity |
| --- | --- |
| `.cursor/skills/`, `~/.cursor/skills/` | `.agents/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/` |
| `~/.cursor/plugins/`, `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | rig installs pstack as skills, not as a plugin. |
| The `SKILL.md` of the `poteto-mode` skill | `<skills>/craft/hub.md`. Put its absolute path in every delegate's `Prompt`. |
| `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, always-applied rules | `~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md` or `.agents/rules/*.md` with `trigger: always_on`, and `GEMINI.md` or `AGENTS.md`. Antigravity never reads `.mdc` files. |
| `https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/<path>` | `<skills>/<name>/<rest>` when `<path>` is `skills/<name>/<rest>` and that file exists. rig does not install `docs/` or `README.md`. Never fetch the URL. Give the user the URL when they need a link. |
| Transcripts in `~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/` | Antigravity keeps each conversation as a SQLite database in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/`, not as a transcript file. Skip a step that reads a transcript and say so. |

### Cursor-only features

Antigravity has no Cursor Automations, Bugbot, Cursor cloud agents, or built-in PR tool. When a step needs one, put one line in your reply, `Skipped in Antigravity: <step>. <reason>.`, then go on to the next step. Do not stop, ask, or retry. When a later step needs what the skipped step made, leave a placeholder and name it in the line. For a PR, use the forge command that the step gives, such as `gh pr create`. That is not a skip.
